researchBackground: Modern vision-language models demonstrate impressive conversational fluency, yet beneath this capability lies a profound fragility: they heavily rely on statistical language priors over perceptual grounding. In my research leading **ThermEval** (accepted at **KDD 2026**), we systematically evaluated 25 foundation models (ranging from 0.3B to 235B parameters, including the Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3 families) on physical thermal imagery. Because thermal imagery encodes physical temperature rather than typical RGB color and texture cues, models cannot rely on surface-level visual shortcuts. The empirical findings were unequivocal: models consistently defaulted to **text-based priors** (such as guessing 'normal' body temperatures) rather than extracting the thermal signal. Crucially, **scaling model capacity did not resolve the benchmark**, and fine-tuning an 8B model still exhibited persistent error floors. Prerequisite structural failures like misinterpreting the colorbar calibration scale, invariably cascaded into severe errors on downstream temperature reasoning. This led to a defining conclusion: *the primary bottleneck in multimodal intelligence is not parameter scale or raw compute, but perceptual grounding itself.*

This disconnect between linguistic fluency and sensory grounding directly motivates the questions at the core of my research. Within **Vision-Language Models & Multimodal Reasoning**, I investigate how architectures can build authentic representations over non-canonical modalities — from continuous physical thermal fields to dense spatial geometries in satellite imagery (as in our Silver Medal-winning **GeoNLI** neuro-symbolic system for ISRO). How can we enforce cross-modal alignment so models reason over sensory evidence rather than hallucinating from linguistic associations? In parallel, this drives my focus on **AI Explainability**: constructing diagnostic, task-ordered evaluation pipelines that isolate precisely *where* multimodal reasoning collapses — from foundational scale calibration to high-level deduction — turning black-box evaluations into verifiable scientific insights.

I have also explored **model compression and inference** — investigating knowledge-based manifold alignment (layer merging on LLaMA-3-8B) and on-device quantization (GGUF) to preserve expressive capacity under aggressive compute limits. Coupled with my experience engineering production AI microservices and high-throughput retrieval pipelines at Barclays, my research philosophy bridges **rigorous empirical science, interpretability, and robust ML systems** to build models that not only reason faithfully, but perform reliably in deployment.
